title: o11ycast - Ep. #80, Augmented Coding with Kent Beck
summary: Kent Beck on 'augmented coding': agents feel like a slot machine, need small steps, tests and observability as reins, misreport and cheat on tests, and let him work in unfamiliar languages.

assertions.quote: this is another theme that's emerging for me is intermittent reinforcement. It's a slot machine.
Oh, you commented out a bunch of tests. We don't do that here.
that's the press release of what I did for you
the limitation on how much change I can let it make at once is how much code I'm willing to look at
Don't like keep betting on a losing hand.
I am doing projects in languages that I've never learned
a senior programmer writes some tests and the junior program goes and makes them pass or whatever. That option is not available anymore

verdicts.note: Plausible and consistent with skill-formation studies and weaker entry-level hiring, but direct evidence on lost apprenticeship tasks is thin.

Anthropic interviews: engineers report losing 'collateral' learning from manual debugging and doc reading, a senior says juniors would need deliberate effort to grow, and juniors ask seniors fewer questions, though one notes they 'learn faster'.
